evals.prompt: Here's a module from our billing service (attached: invoice_utils.py, ~300 lines with a hand-rolled singleton config loader, three near-identical CSV export functions, a bare except around the money math, and a mutable default argument). Clean this up — but we have no tests for it yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs the deterministic detectors first and triages their output; refuses to refactor before pinning behavior (writes/proposes characterization tests per the safety-net rule); flags the bare except and mutable default as correctness bugs, the singleton as ceremony to replace with a module-level instance, and the triplicated exporters as one function; never changes behavior; delivers a findings artifact (list/cards), not just edits, and does not file tickets anywhere without asking.

evals.prompt: my coworker vibe-coded this PR with an llm and i don't trust it. can you review just what changed vs main? repo is checked out here.
evals.expected_output: Uses the diff lens (analyze_diff.py against the merge-base) rather than reviewing the whole repo; runs whole-repo detectors separately only if warranted; loads references/ai-generated-code.md and checks for hallucinated APIs, stubs, fake robustness, and tests that cannot fail; reports findings anchored to changed lines with file:line.

evals.prompt: Is this over-engineered? [pastes a 120-line Python file with an AbstractRepositoryFactory, a single concrete implementation, a Strategy class with one strategy, and a config parameter that is never varied]
evals.expected_output: Judges each abstraction against the over-engineering criteria (single-impl ABC → merge; one-strategy Strategy → plain function; never-varied config → hardcode) with the why, not just the verdict; distinguishes speculative generality from complexity forced by a real requirement; proposes the simpler form concretely.
